rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The respite lets people reform under prophetic guidance and removes their excuse that more time would have changed them; they should use it rather than hasten punishment, whose fixed time cannot be stopped.
rows.anchor: they do not call for the punishment in haste. Its time is fixed; when it will come, no one will be able to stop it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no preparations or repeated command to bring punishment and the Last Day; His single order takes effect in the blink of an eye.
rows.anchor: When He wants to bring it about, He need only order it; not even a repetition of this order will be needed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delay does not make the threat false: earlier nations were destroyed, and people should learn from their fate before events make belief useless.
rows.anchor: it did come on the previous nations that were destroyed by God as a result

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nations called the addressees' counterparts are peoples whose accounts were already recounted in this sūra.
rows.anchor: refers to nations whose anecdotes have been recounted earlier in the sūrah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every deed, whether small or great, is recorded, and God will show each person everything they did.
rows.anchor: Whatever they have done, whether minute or massive has been recorded. God will present to every individual each and everything he had done.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoer will be astonished by the register's exhaustive record of every small or great matter.
rows.anchor: The wrongdoer will cry out about the strange nature of the register which recorded every small or big matter in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The muttaqīn are those who feared standing before God and feared punishment, in contrast to those denying reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: would refer to people who feared being brought into the presence of God and feared punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural 'gardens' signals Paradise's expanse: each person receives several orchards, containing further orchards and smaller gardens.
rows.anchor: the expansive nature of Paradise as well as the fact that each person will be given several orchards

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted muḍāf implies that the righteous are surrounded by the bliss of gardens and rivers.
rows.anchor: an ellipses of the  muḍāf occurs signifying the fact that they will be surrounded in the bliss of orchards and rivers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gardens and rivers belong together; accordingly, Qur'anic references to orchards almost always allude to rivers as well.
rows.anchor: For this reason, almost at every instance in the Qur’ān, whenever an orchard is mentioned, rivers too are alluded to.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers' lasting bliss is an honourable place before the Mighty King; nearness to God is what makes Paradise truly Paradise.
rows.anchor: It is this proximity to God makes Paradise into Paradise otherwise it is nothing more than an orchard.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The annexation of maqʿad to ṣidq conveys permanence and repute, as in the expression lisān ṣidq.
rows.anchor: shows the formers’ permanence and repute just as these meanings are found in the expression

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malīk is more emphatic than milk, and muqtadir strengthens the emphasis further.
rows.anchor: the word ﻣﻠﻴۡﻚ has more emphasis than ﻣﻠْﻚ The attribute ﻣﻘْﺘﺪرٍ further stresses it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not a merely nominal king or a remote being uninvolved in life; He possesses vast dominion.
rows.anchor: regard God to be a remote being who no longer plays any role in their lives; the fact is that He possesses a vast dominion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest honour is a lasting, honourable place near the King of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: an honourable place near the King of the heavens and the earth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of being near God does not mean merging with or becoming God, as some esoteric Sufis claim.
rows.anchor: He will never merge into God and become God as is claimed by some esoteric sufis.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The previous sūra answered the People of the Book's objection to jihād; hypocrites then spread opponents' objections among Muslims to weaken faith and suppress zeal for jihād.
rows.anchor: The previous sūrah ended with the answer to the objection raised by the People of the Book against jihād.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra checks clandestine anti-Islamic propaganda, reprimands the hypocrites, and directs Muslims to take measures; it also models sincerely bringing a difficulty to the Prophet and trusting God to resolve it.
rows.anchor: the hypocrites are severely reprimanded for indulging in such subversive activities, and in order to curb them, Muslims are also directed to adopt certain measures.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pious woman presented her religious difficulty to God and the Prophet with trust rather than frustration; God resolved it and made her response a Qur'anic example of proper conduct in hardship.
rows.anchor: The Almighty resolved her difficulty and set her forth as an example in the Qur’ ān: the example of a person who adopted the correct attitude when troubles came her way.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who use real or hypothetical difficulty as a pretext for anti-Islamic propaganda open a war front against God and His Messenger, face humiliation, and cannot prevail over God's and the prophets' cause.
rows.anchor: It is the incontestable decision of God that success and dominance is only reserved for God and His prophets.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites whisper evil suggestions to others and malign Islam's cause.
rows.anchor: busy whispering evil suggestions to others and maligning the cause of Islam.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites disrespected the Prophet and treated God's forbearance in not punishing them as proof of their own correctness.
rows.anchor: by not punishing them as a proof of their correct attitude.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are warned of humiliation in this world, as history shows, and grievous punishment in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: they shall not only be humiliated in this world as history testifies, but will also face a grievous torment in the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims must avoid sin and excess and keep private conversation clean and pious rather than speaking against the Prophet.
rows.anchor: their secret conversations should not be against the Prophet (sws); their intimate exchanges should be clean and pious.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocritical whispering can harm no one without God's permission, so believers should trust their Lord and rely on His protection.
rows.anchor: such whispering cannot harm anyone unless the Almighty permits it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must observe proper manners in the Prophet's company and avoid clandestine conversation around him; temporary directives were issued to curb the hypocrites' whispering.
rows.anchor: and forbidden to carry out clandestine conversation when they are gathered around him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the emergency measures achieved their purpose, they were repealed and believers were directed to establish worship practices to end whispering and secret conversation.
rows.anchor: After the achievement of the desired results, the emergency directives have been repealed and the believers have been directed to establish those forms of worship

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites are agents of the Jews, who incurred God's wrath, and their true allegiance lies with them.
rows.anchor: the hypocrites are actually the agents of the Jews who have incurred the wrath of the Almighty; their real allegiance rests with them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oaths and glibness conceal the hypocrites' real character, allowing them to appear Muslim while serving Islam's enemies.
rows.anchor: Their glibness and their trait of swearing during conversation effectively conceals their real character and they are able to outwardly show themselves as Muslims.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love of wealth and Satan's influence make them heedless and part of his party, obstructing the Prophet's mission; their efforts fail because God has decreed that He and His prophets prevail.
rows.anchor: Satan has made them unmindful of God and they have joined his party to impair and obstruct the Prophet’s mission; ultimately their efforts shall fizzle out

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True believers sever ties with God's and the Prophet's enemies even when they are close relatives; God is pleased with them, they belong to His party, and they alone succeed.
rows.anchor: True believers are those who sever their ties of relationship from the enemies of God and the Prophet (sws) even if they are their fathers, sons, brothers and tribesmen.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, samiʿa means both hearing and accepting; the author notes this Qur'anic and common Arabic usage, also familiar in ordinary speech.
rows.anchor: They also signify acceptance. It has been used in this meaning in the Qur’ān, and this meaning is common in the Arabic language as well.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An incomplete verb is elided before tujādiluka under Arabic grammatical principles, indicating that the woman repeatedly came to the Prophet to tell her story.
rows.anchor: a suppression of an incomplete verb has occurred as per the general principles of Arabic language.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mujādalah can be negative quibbling or quarrelling, but positively it means persuading through affection, pleading, insistence, and fondness.
rows.anchor: When used negatively, it refers to quibble and to quarrel. When used positively, it refers to convince someone through affection, pleading, insistence and fondness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's affectionate, trusting argument with God about Lot's people is an example of this positive form of argument, and God praised it.
rows.anchor: which he had with His Lord regarding the people of Lot (sws). The Almighty praised it
